caption: The drawing displays a technical illustration of a kitchen chair in black ink on a beige background. It includes three main views: a front elevation, a side elevation, and a top-down view of the seat. The front elevation, located in the lower left, shows a chair with a curved backrest supported by four vertical spindles and two outer slightly angled back legs. The seat has a rectangular profile, and four turned legs are connected by crossbars. The side elevation, at the lower right, reveals the angle of the backrest, the curved top rail, and the outwardly splayed legs, with measured heights for each segment. The top-down view, at the upper center, presents the seat shape with rounded and indented sides, supplying width and depth measurements. Various dimensions are marked in inches alongside arrows, such as the seat being 13½ inches wide and 13¾ inches deep, a total chair height of 32½ inches, and distances between legs. In the upper right, there is a title block identifying the item as a "Kitchen Chair" and referencing the New York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West, with the number 2139-B written below. The drawing contains no shading or color except for the black ink on a beige surface.
title: Kitchen Chair
